clue.text: Clerk’s content - after small slummy pad it will be digs for him

definitions.text: it will be digs for him

indicators.note: the content of a word is what sits inside it, so only its inner letters are kept

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a hovel is a squalid little dwelling
the word clerk without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A clerk resigned to living in a squalid little flat, which will be his lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: The clerk's insides go after S and HOVEL even though they come first in the clue. 'Digs' plays on lodgings (the hovel) and on shovelling; the SHOVELLER is also a duck, one of the puzzle's many birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wields a spade spends the day digging, so the job of shifting earth falls to him.

clue.text: Move around aimlessly, pale and sickly following sun

indicators.note: following says the piece before it in the clue comes after the next one in the answer

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for sun
wan means pallid and unwell-looking

explanation.surface: Someone pale and ill wanders about after too long in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following sun' means the WAN part comes after S.
explanation.definitionFit: To swan around is a British idiom for wandering about idly, often showily, with no real purpose.

clue.text: A plover flying - it will cross the gap

indicators.note: a bird in flight is all over the place, so the letters before it are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wading bird takes off and flies across a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Where two edges extend past each other they span the space between, so the join covers any opening.

clue.text: Final part mutated in core of certain glands

indicators.note: something mutated has changed form, so the following letters take a different order

blocks.note: the end is the final part of anything
taken as written: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The last part of something has mutated in the core of certain glands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Core' looks like the hidden-letters signal, but the word itself is part of the anagram fodder with 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ductless glands releasing hormones straight into the blood make up the hormone system, so the adjective describes those glands.

clue.text: Play about a city Romeo ending in heartbreak

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles, a city
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the last letter of heartbreak

explanation.surface: A city Romeo fools around, and it ends in heartbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo suggests a philanderer here, but it is just the radio code word for R.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is to fool around in a playful, mischievous way; the word is also a songbird.

clue.text: Little critters chewed acorns round Colorado

indicators.note: something chewed is mangled, so the letters of the next word are jumbled
round means placed around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written: the letters to rearrange
CO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Colorado

explanation.surface: Small animals gnawed acorns somewhere around Colorado.
explanation.definitionFit: These masked North American mammals are small furry animals, informally called critters in American speech.

clue.text: High level of support initially seen on pitch

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the first letter of seen
to pitch is to tilt or slope

explanation.surface: Strong support for the team showed first on the football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a sports field; here it means a slope or lean. The answer is also a long-legged wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole with a footrest raises a walker or a building well above the ground, holding it up at height.

clue.text: Going over, step inside, entirely inside - maybe a long shot

indicators.note: the letters sit wholly within the run of clue words, not spilling outside them
in a down clue, going over means reading upward, so the letters are taken in reverse

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Instructions to step in and stay right inside as something goes over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' is part of the hiding place as well as a signal word, which makes the run hard to spot. The answer is also a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper's shot is fired from far off at a hidden target, so a single such shot may well be a long-range one.

clue.text: Russian boy with weedkiller becomes a ‘Scottish’ hero?

blocks.note: Ivan is a typical Russian boy's name
a hoe is a garden tool for killing weeds

explanation.surface: A Russian lad armed with herbicide is somehow hailed as a Scottish hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks and question mark flag that the hero is English: he is 'Scottish' only because Sir Walter Scott wrote him.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Walter Scott's 1819 novel is a Saxon knight, a hero created by a Scottish author.

clue.text: The last question in a row - is a beer drunk with Kelvin?

indicators.note: a drunk person is unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order
in tells us one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written: letters to rearrange
K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A pub quiz-master asks whether, in a row of drinks, a beer goes down with someone called Kelvin.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters go inside TIER, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: When a quiz ends level, a deciding extra question settles the winner, so it is asked at the very end.

clue.text: I agree with the German editor

blocks.note: amen is said to express agreement
der is the German masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Someone concurs with the German editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who revises a text and corrects its errors is doing the work of altering and improving it.

clue.text: Cold capital city on limits of the normal weather

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two outermost letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Lima is the capital of Peru
the first and last letters of the

explanation.surface: A cold capital city sits at the edge of normal weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The prevailing conditions of a region measured over many years form its long-term pattern rather than any single day's forecast.

clue.text: Some sheep wool patterned onto cloth

blocks.note: first meaning: a group of sheep kept together
second meaning: fibres stuck onto fabric or paper to make a raised pattern

explanation.surface: A description of woollen cloth decorated with sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the velvety raised pattern of flock wallpaper, made from short wool fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both a herd of grazing animals and the tufts of fibre glued to fabric for a raised design.

clue.text: Zero gravity? - held by secure cord with something else

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped within it, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: zero looks like the letter O
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity
a tether is a rope that keeps something secured

explanation.surface: An astronaut floating in zero gravity is kept safe by a cord.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a thing in company means doing it jointly, accompanied by another person or object.

clue.text: Fast percussion playing

indicators.note: music being played moves its notes about, so the letters are performed in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drummer playing at high speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling quicker than the speed of sound is about as quick as an aircraft gets, so the adjective means very rapid.

clue.text: Around 1st of Nov increase assistance for free

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
around means wrapped about, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to up something is to increase it
the opening letter of Nov
aid is help or assistance

explanation.surface: From early November, support increases, given without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done without wages is voluntary, carried out without receiving any money in return.

clue.text: Privately eccentric cinema artist

indicators.note: an eccentric is odd and off-centre, so the next word's letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written: letters to rearrange
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An odd film-maker who likes to work in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase describes court hearings held in a judge's chambers, away from the public, so it means secretly.

clue.text: It thickens line on castle that’s a bit short in drawing

indicators.note: falling a bit short means losing a little at the end, so the last letter goes
in tells us the pieces before it go inside the next word

blocks.note: a row is a line
the rook is the castle in chess
drawing is a form of art

explanation.surface: A line drawn on a castle in a sketch that's slightly too short.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above. 'Drawing' reads as a sketch, and the castle is the chess piece, not a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: The starch from this tropical plant's root is used in cooking to make sauces and gravies set firmer.

clue.text: Poetic hero Sheila’s regularly seen with a battered hat

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
something battered is knocked out of shape, so its letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
W is an abbreviation for with
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A heroic figure from verse seen beside a woman wearing a battered hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A sheila is Australian slang for a woman, but here the name only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow's 1855 narrative poem 'The Song of Hiawatha' has this Ojibwe warrior as its central figure.

clue.text: Arcane oddball coteries

indicators.note: an oddball is strange and out of the ordinary, so the next word's letters are made odd

blocks.note: taken as written: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Strange, eccentric little cliques with mysterious ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge understood only by a small initiated group is obscure and mysterious to everyone outside it.

clue.text: Essentially vocal rain dances for wind instrument

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept
letters that dance move about, so the next word is rearranged

blocks.note: the three central letters of vocal
taken as written: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sung rain dance accompanied by a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This small egg-shaped flute, often of clay, is played by blowing, which makes it a woodwind-type instrument.

clue.text: Grey example of river carp

blocks.note: GR is a dictionary abbreviation for grey
the Ouse is one of several English rivers of that name

explanation.surface: A grey fish from the river, a carp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the fish to match the river, but it is the verb: to complain. The answer is also a game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault and complain, and to grouse is likewise to grumble about something.

clue.text: Confined with no food’s intrinsically concerning

indicators.note: intrinsically means at its heart, so the next piece goes into the middle of the previous one

blocks.note: unfed means not given food
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone locked up without food, which is worrying in itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone never released from captivity remains locked up, still imprisoned and not at liberty.

clue.text: Falls for regressive regulations leading to depressions

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the next word is read from its end

blocks.note: laws are regulations
lows are depressions, in weather or mood

explanation.surface: Waterfalls tumbling into hollows, governed by backward rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like waterfalls; here it is the verb in 'falls for', to be taken in. The answer is also a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a story whole without question is to be fooled by it, as a credulous listener is.

clue.text: Feudal lord for instance in fiction

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for instance
a fiction is an untruth

explanation.surface: A medieval lord appears in a story, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiction' suggests a novel; here it means a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the feudal system a vassal owed loyalty and service to his superior, the master he swore allegiance to.

clue.text: Street’s internet access mostly high-speed

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
the apostrophe s stands for has, as in holding something inside

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
wi-fi is wireless internet access

explanation.surface: A street whose wi-fi is mostly fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Wi-fi loses its last letter and sits between the two letters of ST. The answer is also a fast-flying bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Something quick-moving travels at great pace, so rapid and fast describe it equally.

clue.text: Equipment that’s electronic - it’s used to test opinions

blocks.note: kit is gear or equipment
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: An electronic device used for polling people's views.
explanation.walkthrough: To fly a kite is to float an idea and see how people react. The answer is also a bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial balloon is floated to gauge public reaction before committing, which is what a flown kite does.

clue.text: Wordgame is insubstantial but not “beginning with W”

indicators.note: but not removes what follows, here the opening letter W

blocks.note: wispy means thin and insubstantial

explanation.surface: A word game judged flimsy, unless it begins with W.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase echoes the game's own call, 'something beginning with...', which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's guessing game has players name objects starting with a given letter, so it is played with words.

clue.text: Most primitive indigenous peoples having time to move east

indicators.note: in an across clue east is the right-hand end, so the letter is taken out and placed at the end

blocks.note: natives are indigenous peoples
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The most basic native tribes have time to migrate eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: Simplest and least sophisticated describes the most unrefined, untutored art or person, the furthest from worldly.

clue.text: One SW county has 25% off similar compounds

indicators.note: a quarter off means a quarter of the letters, two of eight, are dropped from the end

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Somerset is a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: A south-western county with a quarter off its price.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset has eight letters, so 25% off removes the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, molecules with identical formulas but different atomic arrangements are closely related substances.

clue.text: To some extent when arch goes over winch is required

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the words, so the letters sit within them
going over means turning back, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: When building an arch, a lifting winch is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a long-legged wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine for hoisting heavy loads with a cable and drum does the lifting work of a winch.

clue.text: Dealt very roughly as a preventative measure

indicators.note: roughly means carelessly handled, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone handled harshly as a precaution.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting so as to ward something off turns it away beforehand, which is what a precaution does.
